summary: Head-of-list lens (ranks 1-10) on the 7,214-feed discovery half (base NDCG 0.39939). I submit zero rules because nothing reaches a cross-fitted gain of +0.0003 with z >= 2. I tried about 1,250 parameter settings in about 20 rule families. The opportunity is real: a perfect re-order of the top 10, with the head set fixed, would add +0.21 NDCG (top 3: +0.056). But the columns cannot find it. A cross-fitted LightGBM head re-ranker loses 0.0022-0.0052. A residual GBM loses more the longer it trains (-0.00004 at 50 rounds, -0.0016 at 400). A ridge conditional logit over all 46 columns loses 0.0011-0.0030. In 308 quintile bins of 35 features there is no bin where rank 2 beats rank 1, and cross-fitted swap trees for 1<->2, 2<->3 and 1<->3 are all <= 0 out of fold. The branch weight is already optimal at 0.5/0.5 (0.6: +0.00001). Re-weighting toward s_to inside the head costs 0.0005-0.0011. Per-segment branch weights, cross-fitted over 7 segmentations, range from -0.0006 to +0.00014 (in-sample +0.0002 to +0.0005, which is fold noise). Where the branches disagree on top-1 (1,378 feeds), the consensus is right most often (9.0% vs 8.6% ft and 7.5% to). Within-feed choice models find only weak single-feature signals (max z about 2.9 at K=10, which is the null level). The strong-looking residuals in rank-calibrated tables (hmean5 z=6.2, category share z=6.6) are either feed-level confounds or sit in the middle/tail, so they do not move NDCG. The closest failures: an h10 tie-break at w=-0.02, cross-fitted +0.00052 (z 1.95, one of about 600 tie-break variants); a boost for very popular items (popularity-only), +0.00048 (z 1.57); a hmax boost in small feeds, +0.00047 (z 1.67).

summary:
Category lens: no rule submitted (rules/ is empty on purpose). I tested about 377 rule families, about 2,650 parameter variants in all. Each was scored by cross-fitted NDCG over kit.folds on 7,214 feeds. None reached +0.0003 with z >= 2. The best honest results were +0.0002 to +0.0004 with z 1.0-2.0. Given how many families were tried, that is what noise looks like.

Category-level calibration is good. A conditional logit over the categories of each feed gives a model-mass coefficient of 1.00-1.04. By vertical, O/E runs from 0.93 to 1.03, and every leaf category has |z| <= 2.2. Re-fitting category mass with extra state features hurts NDCG even in sample (-0.0001 to -0.0002).

There are real likelihood signals:
- feed share of the category (score-test z +5.6)
- history share, f3
- the newest event's category at ranks 1-3 (O/E 1.08 against 0.87 for categories last seen 5-31 events ago)
- Services over-ranked (O/E 0.93 overall, 0.72 when the user has no Services history)

None of them turns into NDCG. They sit in the tail or reverse from fold to fold. For example, the feed-share boost scores -0.00064 cross-fitted, and head boosts of the newest event's category score -0.0001 to -0.0004.

The only consistent near-miss is a global Services demotion of -0.1 z-units: +0.00022, SE 0.00022, z 1.0. Its per-fold deltas are +.00063/-.00008/+.00011/+.00014/+.00029, so it is not submitted.

Two flexible upper bounds also fail out of fold:
- a LightGBM lambdarank residual on category and all features (18 configurations): -0.0002 to -0.010
- a ridge linear LambdaRank on 41 category features: -0.0013 to -0.0025, and negative in sample too

On this sample the model uses the category structure about as well as it can be used. In bad feeds, the positive is mostly deep inside a category the model already favours, with lower similarity than the head. Those look like choices driven by photo or price, which the features cannot see.

summary: I am submitting no rules: nothing in this lens survived cross-fitting. On the discovery sample (7,214 feeds, 11,026 positives, base NDCG 0.39939) the model already orders items inside a category and among near-duplicates about as well as these columns allow. A conditional logit inside (feed, category) groups that contain a positive (8,306 groups, 31 features, score as offset) found no effect beyond |z| 2.7 (z 3.1 when only groups of 30+ candidates are kept). 660 segment-specific within-category slopes peaked at |z| 3.77, which is what chance gives for 660 tests. About 120 observed/expected cells in the top-10 are all within |z| 1.9. In near-duplicate pairs (found exactly as two rows of a feed with equal cand_maxcos; 1,572 pairs with one positive), the score picks the clicked member 58-61% of the time. Once the score is known, freshness, popularity and closeness to the newest event add nothing reliable (f4 z -1.7). The only strong signals are listwise-likelihood miscalibrations in the tail of the list: category size (z 5.5), category share of history (z 5.3), and within-category score spread growing with category size (z 6.3). They also improve the out-of-fold likelihood (+0.0026 nats per feed, z 2.95), but they lower NDCG (-0.00042). Across about 185 cross-fitted NDCG variants, the best out-of-fold results were +0.00011 (z 1.76, more weight on the train-only branch for categories absent from history) and +0.00010 (z 1.5, boosting near-copies); both fall short of the +0.0003 and z 2 bar. Learned head re-rankers fitted on 4 folds (conditional logit, NDCG-weighted pairwise, and LightGBM lambdarank on the residual) were all at or below zero on the held-out fold, down to -0.0116 for the largest LightGBM.

findings.finding: Inside a category, the clicked item cannot be told apart from its category mates once the model score is accounted for.
findings.evidence: Conditional logit inside (feed, category) groups with a positive (8,306 groups, 10,473 positives), one feature at a time with the score as offset: max effect h32 +0.049/sd (z 2.7), then xp_imp_c50 -0.030 (z -2.6); all others |z| < 1.9 (screen_within.py). Observed/expected by within-category quintile for 19 features in categories with 10+ candidates is flat within +-6% (desc3.py). 660 segment x feature within-category slope tests: max |z| 3.77 (furniture, freshness), consistent with chance (screen_inter.py).

All ~120 cells have |z| <= 1.9: hmax band x hmax_idx band, hmax_type/src, dup count, f4/f5 quintiles, exposure band, cat_user_rank, within-category rank, c_contact/c_fav/c_vfeed >= .95, n_hdup95, same_cat_newest, cat_newest_idx band, h1 band, category share x M, newest_type, category code. NDCG-weighted pairwise logistic on same-category pairs in the top-10/30 with feed-clustered SEs: max |z| 2.0 (pairs_head.py).

findings.finding: Near-duplicate pairs can be identified exactly. The model's score already picks the clicked member, and duplicates are not diluted.
findings.evidence: Rows of a feed with equal cand_maxcos are mutual nearest pairs (56,243 pairs; 29,768 isolated). In the 1,572 pairs with exactly one positive, the higher-scored member is the clicked one 58% (cos .95-.98), 61% (.98-.995) and 61% (>= .995) of the time. The clicked member is fresher in 47.6% / 47.0% / 39.3% of pairs (z -1.6, -1.3, -1.7); given the score, f4 is -0.07/sd (z -1.7) (pairs_sign.py, pairs.py). Top-10 O/E for the lower member of a pair whose partner ranks above it: 1.10 (z 1.2); upper member 1.04-1.12 (head_dupabove.py).

findings.finding: The within-category score spread is miscalibrated by category size: too compressed in big categories, too wide in small ones. The effect is real but sits in the tail and does not move NDCG.
findings.evidence: Full-list conditional logit z = a*s + (b0 + b1*log cat_n)*(s - category mean of s): b0 -0.239 (z -5.3), b1 +0.083 (z +6.3). In the newest event's category the extra spread is +0.115 (z 4.5) (fit_scale.py, screen_scale.py). Out of fold: log-likelihood +0.0026 nats per feed (z 2.95), but NDCG -0.00042 (z -1.0) (t_oofll.py). Restricted to the top-10/20 the effect is only z 1.6-2.0 (fit_scale_head.py). Cross-fitted stretch rule, 15 variants: -0.00031.

findings.finding: Category size, history share and near-duplicate count are under-weighted in listwise likelihood, but correcting them lowers NDCG. The gains are at deep ranks, and the head is calibrated.
findings.evidence: Full-list conditional logit: lcatn +0.097/sd (z 5.5), cat_hist_share +0.073 (z 5.3), ldup +0.030 (z 2.6). Out-of-fold log-likelihood gains are z 2.05 / 2.11 / 1.05, while NDCG changes by -0.00016 / -0.00019 / -0.00089. Additive cross-fits: lcatn -0.00024, cat_hist_share -0.00039, ldup -0.00008. The raw table of top-of-list click rate by category share is confounded by feed size and flat for M >= 100.

summary:
I am submitting zero rules from the segments / score-shape lens. On the 7,214 discovery feeds (base NDCG 0.39939), nothing reached the bar of a cross-fitted gain of at least +0.0003 with z of at least 2. I tried about 1,870 variants in roughly 60 families.

Segment-specific blends of the score with simple signals do not help. I tested 27 signals across these segments: M, H, hour, weekday, n_feed_cats, newest_type, guest/cold users, contact-heavy histories, score peakedness and branch correlation. The cross-fitted deltas are almost all negative, with a mean of -4e-4 over a 144-variant lens scan. Only one variant reached z > 2, and it was noise from 181 guest feeds.

Re-weighting the two branches (s_ft vs s_to) gives a jagged curve with its optimum at 0.5 in every segment. The two branches correlate at a median of 0.993 within a feed. Other ways of combining them (disagreement penalties, rank fusion, soft-min/max) also do not help.

As a headroom check, residual LightGBM rankers with the model score as init were also negative in every setting: -22 to -65 (lambdarank) and +0.4 to -6.1 (pointwise), in units of 1e-4. Category-specific slopes, segment x category offsets and head-only re-orderings were all negative too.

Good and bad feeds differ in a clear way. In feeds with at least 60 candidates where the best positive is at rank 30 or worse, that positive:
- is the median 12th item of a 28-candidate category;
- shares the top-1 item's category in only 28% of feeds (83% in good feeds);
- comes from a category absent from history 11% of the time (3% in good feeds);
- is weaker on every affinity signal (f3 0.48 vs 0.66, h1 0.53 vs 0.70).

The model's score peakedness hardly differs between good and bad feeds (g110 0.76 vs 0.84), so it cannot flag them.

The best near-miss is a within-category saturation penalty: score - 0.02*(cat_rank_in_feed-1)^0.3. It gains +2.3e-4 cross-fitted (z 2.5), and the per-fold deltas range from -0.2 to +5.1. It is the best of about 160 variants in its family. A likelihood check restricted to the head does not corroborate it. It is saved at <repo>/lab/nn_x/errfix_1117/agents/segments/work/candidate_cat_saturation.py and is not submitted. Full notes are in <repo>/lab/nn_x/errfix_1117/agents/segments/notes.txt.

summary: I am submitting no rules. Within the recent-intent lens, FD16P20 has no ranking error I could find. I analysed the 7,214 discovery feeds (base NDCG 0.39939). For h1, h5, h10, hmean5, the event-typed similarities (c_*) and cat_newest_idx, observed/expected positive rates stay within 0.93-1.07 in every bin with 200+ positives. The expected rate comes from a within-feed softmax of the score with slope 0.98, so the score already behaves as a calibrated log-odds. Some residuals do hold up. Top-10 items whose mean similarity to the last 5 history events (hmean5) is at least 0.8 are under-predicted in all 5 folds (O/E 1.09-1.20, about 750 positives). In large feeds (M >= 150), recency is under-weighted on likelihood (z +4.4 to +4.8). After a contact, near-copies of contacted items have O/E 1.18. All three are size-of-score effects, not ordering errors. In 13,647 head pairs with a score gap under 0.05 and exactly one positive, the upper item is positive 49.9% of the time, and no lens feature tells which one is positive (|z| at most 2.3; all lean slightly towards the item less like recent history). I tried 108 cross-fitted rule variants plus 20 residual-GBM configurations. The best was a tiny demotion of items similar to feed-viewed items (oof +0.00039, z 1.97). That is within the null: 40 random features gave oof up to +0.00051 and z up to 1.88. The residual GBMs reached at most +0.00009, and a per-group s_ft/s_to re-weighting gave -0.00040. Positives the model misses (rank 31+) sit in large feeds and look less like the history: median h1 0.52 vs 0.69 at ranks 1-3, and 10% vs 3.3% in a category absent from the history. They are clicks the history does not predict, not a pattern a rule can fix.

findings.finding: The score is a calibrated within-feed log-odds, and the lens features show no marginal miscalibration.
findings.evidence: A conditional logit on the score alone has slope 0.98; adding s_ft/s_to separately or quadratic terms changes the negative log-likelihood by under 0.5. O/E by bin of h1, h5, h10, hmean5, hmax, c_contact, c_order, c_fav, c_lead, c_vfeed, c_vsearch, cat_newest_idx and same_cat_newest is within 0.93-1.07 in every bin with 200+ positives (resid1.py, resid2.py).

In top-10 pairs where exactly one item has hmean5 >= 0.8 and the gap is < 0.1, the upper item is positive 0.495 vs 0.488 and 0.536 vs 0.545 of the time. The excess comes from pairs with a gap > 0.4 (0.77 vs 0.59). Every boost form is negative or zero under cross-fitting (best oof +0.00013, z 0.6).

findings.evidence: There are 13,647 pairs (top 30, gap < 0.05, one positive) in 3,679 feeds, and the upper item is positive 49.9% of the time. For each feature, z of the mean sign(feature difference) x outcome, clustered by feed: hmean5 -2.1, c_contact -2.3, same_cat_newest -2.0, h1 -1.6, h10 -1.0. All 34 features have |z| < 2.3. A composite novelty tie-breaker gives oof -0.00005 (neartie.py, t_novelty.py).

findings.evidence: For M >= 150, the clogit score test gives z +4.8 for cat_newest_idx <= 5 and +4.3/+4.4 for h1/h10/hmean5; these hold up after about 1,300 tests. The fitted shift is only 0.07-0.09 score units per within-feed SD and acts in the tail. The cross-fitted NDCG of 24 forms ranges from -0.00019 to +0.00013 (t_bigM.py, t_coef.py).

After a view from search or another surface, near-copies of that item are clicked less (they were probably already seen on the results page). Neither can be used.

summary: No rules submitted. On the popularity, exposure, freshness and cold columns the model is already close to optimal, and every correction I tried failed out of sample. Discovery base NDCG is 0.39939 on 7,214 feeds. One-dimensional calibration is flat: A/E (actual vs expected positives) stays within 0.89-1.14 for every bin of xp_imp_c50, f4, f5, it_hist_*, seq_cv and pre2. The one systematic deviation is that the head is over-confident (A/E 0.934 at rank 1, 1.064 at ranks 11-20), which does not change the order. Learned upper-bound probes gave nothing usable: LightGBM on top of the score reached at best +0.0005 (z 0.9), regularised conditional logit at best +0.00017, and a head-only re-ranker was -0.0002 to -0.0024. I tried about 730 rule variants (25+ families). Each family has its own cross-fit, but choosing the family and weight together on 4 folds gives -0.00011, -0.00087, -0.00024 and -0.00063 on four fold seeds, so the in-sample winners are selection noise. A simulation shows why. Even the strongest real likelihood effect, cold listings in categories the user browsed 50+ times (beta +0.139, z 3.4), would give only +0.00027 expected NDCG if fully true, which is below the +0.0003 bar. The other effects (fresh vacancies/services, low f5 at high exposure, cold items in the user's top category) would give +0.00005 to +0.00009. Several hypotheses from the brief did not hold: high f5 at low exposure is not over-trusted, the encoder scores are not mis-trusted on cold items, and no segment prefers a branch mix other than 0.5/0.5. The best near-miss is kept, unsubmitted, as <repo>/lab/nn_x/errfix_1117/agents/popularity_fresh/work/rejected_cold_heavycat.py (in-sample +0.00068, z 2.52), with the reasons in the file and in <repo>/lab/nn_x/errfix_1117/agents/popularity_fresh/notes.txt.

findings.finding: The model is well calibrated along every column in this lens. The only deviation is a head temperature effect (over-confident at the top), and it cannot change the order.
findings.evidence: A/E by bin: xp_imp_c50 0.94-1.02, f4 0.89-1.07, f5 0.97-1.08, it_hist_* 0.93-1.07, seq_cv 0.94-1.04, pre2 0.94-1.14. By rank: rank 1 0.934, ranks 2-3 0.946, ranks 11-20 1.064. The softmax temperature that maximises likelihood is exactly 1.0 (work/a01_resid.py, a09_head.py).

LightGBM binary or lambdarank without score features: at best +0.00049 (z 0.94). Conditional logit with offset=score, 19/159/100/240 features: at best +0.00017; the lens-only fit is -0.0004 even in-sample. Head-only re-ranking (top 5/10/20): -0.0002 to -0.0024.

findings.evidence: Nested cross-fit choosing family and weight together on 4 folds (25 families, 128 candidates): -0.00011 (seed 0), -0.00087, -0.00024, -0.00063 (seeds 1-3). Lambda-gradient screen: 588 tests, z sd 1.34, 21 with |z|>3, close to the null (work/a21_nested.py, a06_screen.py).

findings.finding: Effects that are real at the likelihood level are too small, or sit too far down the list, to pay in NDCG. To clear +0.0003, an effect needs |beta| above roughly 0.3 on items competing for the top 5, and none exists in this lens.

summary: I am submitting zero rules. On the discovery half (7,214 feeds, base NDCG 0.399392), I could not find a learned residual on top of the FD16P20 score that gains anything when cross-fitted on kit.folds. LightGBM residuals used init_score = 1.0*score (the softmax scale fitted on the training folds), 130 raw and within-feed derived columns, and lambdarank, binary or a custom per-feed softmax objective. They all score at or below 0 out of fold. The best was +0.00037 (z 0.8, regularised lambdarank at 10 trees), and runs reached -0.012 at 400 trees, while in-sample fit reached +0.037. Linear and binned (857 dummies) conditional-logit residuals score -0.0010 to -0.0114. The tree learners are also weak at this sample size: starting from s_to (-0.00113) with s_ft and s_ft-s_to available, they win back at most half the gap (to -0.0006). Their noise costs about 0.0005-0.001, so the measured upper bound for a feature rule here is about 0. Simpler versions do no better. One-term nudges (96 columns, weights by MLE or by an NDCG grid inside the cross-fit) behave like random columns: mean z -0.45 for real columns against -0.28 for random ones. Nested greedy forward selection, which repeats the whole scan inside each fold, loses NDCG: -0.00071 (z -2.4) after one term and -0.00143 after three. Its first pick differed in four of five folds, with +0.0005 to +0.0009 gains on the training folds, which shows how large the selection bias is. Calibration scans also look like noise: about 1,500 feature bins (max |z| 3.4) and 1,279 category-by-context cells (4 with |z|>=2.8 against 6.5 expected by chance). Badly ranked feeds are mostly large (median M 167 against 29 for good feeds). Their deep positives are exploration clicks with low recent-history similarity, while the rank-1 negatives look just like the positives in good feeds. Over about 300 cross-fitted variants, the nearest misses were +0.00029 with z 1.89 and +0.00029 with z 2.12 (the second on a segment I picked in-sample). Neither meets the bar.

Regularised lambdarank (7 leaves, min_data 3000, l2 100): best +0.00037 (z 0.8). Binary 4 leaves: best +0.00022 (z 1.7). Per-feed softmax objective with 3 leaves and min_data 20000: best +0.00014 (z 1.2). Restricting to one feature group (sim/pop/cat/ctx): best +0.00026 (z 0.7). Linear conditional logit: -0.0010 (in-sample only +0.00047). Binned GAM: -0.0011 to -0.0114. All runs are in cv_log.txt.

summary:
I found nothing systematic in the model's confident errors, and I submitted one weak rule that is probably noise.

I read 45 lens-(a) feeds (rank 1 negative, gap to rank 2 in the top quartile, best positive at 30 or lower), 25 lens-(b) feeds (positive at rank 50+ with fewer than 120 candidates), 12 small bad feeds in full and 25 good feeds. I then tested 8 behavioural hypotheses on all 7,214 discovery feeds.

- **The head is calibrated.** Rank-1 precision rises with the gap to rank 2: 20.3% vs 8.3% for rank 2 in the top gap quintile. In none of 25 head segments does rank 2 beat rank 1, so no swap rule exists.
- **Matched comparison.** At matched score (each positive against its ±3 rank neighbours), no column separates positives from negatives beyond about |z| 3. That is noise level for about 180 tests.
- **Residual model.** A LightGBM boosted from the model's own score, cross-fitted by user, gains at most +0.00023 (z 0.6); larger versions lose up to -0.0025. Free stackers lose -0.006 to -0.011.
- **Simple rules.** All 28 single-column corrections and all branch re-weightings or uncertainty bonuses are ≤ +0.0003 cross-fitted.
- **Submitted rule.** The best of 144 segment × feature pairs is small feeds (M < 40) × the within-feed z-score of hmax, at weight 0.05. Cross-fitted it gives +0.00074, SE 0.00031, z 2.39, with the same weight chosen in all 5 folds. That clears the thresholds only nominally: after picking the best of 144 pairs it is more likely noise than not, and its gain peaks sharply at w = 0.05.
- **Item prior from discovery labels (the data idea).** Real but small. Items positive in another user's feed have O/E 1.79, but they are only 0.19% of rows here (0.33% on test). The best rule gives +0.00057 cross-fitted, z 1.82. It is not submitted because it needs validation labels when applied.

In total I ran about 1,900 evaluations covering about 230 distinct forms.
